questions.stem: The graph of y = f(x) is translated to give y = f(x) + 3. This is a translation of:
questions.explanation: y = f(x) + 3 adds 3 to every y-value, shifting the graph 3 units up.

questions.stem: The graph of y = x^2 is transformed to y = (x - 4)^2. What happens to the turning point?
questions.explanation: y = f(x - 4) is a translation 4 units to the right. So (0, 0) moves to (4, 0). Note: the minus sign inside the bracket gives a positive shift.

questions.stem: If the point (2, 5) is on y = f(x), what point is on y = f(-x)?
questions.explanation: y = f(-x) is a reflection in the y-axis. The x-coordinate changes sign: (2, 5) becomes (-2, 5).

questions.stem: y = -f(x) is a transformation of y = f(x). What type of transformation is it?

options.text: Stretch by scale factor -1 in the x-direction

questions.explanation: y = -f(x) multiplies all y-values by -1, which reflects the graph in the x-axis.

questions.stem: The graph y = f(x) has a maximum point at (3, 7). What is the maximum point of y = 2f(x)?
questions.explanation: y = 2f(x) stretches the graph vertically by a factor of 2. The x-coordinates stay the same; the y-coordinates are doubled. So (3, 7) becomes (3, 14).
